# `bin/watch-run`

A tool: run it from the root of an instance (or of the kit, for the kit's own tools).
Source: [`bin/watch-run`](../../../bin/watch-run)

## What it says about itself

```text
bin/watch-run RUN [-f] [--last N] [--full] [--thinking]

Human-readable view of a run's transcript (Claude Code stream-json or Codex events). Read-only.
  RUN         run name (005-attack-audit), a run directory, or a path to a launch log. Reads Claude Code's
              launch.log and Codex's launch.jsonl, from .claude/state/ext/RUN/logs/ while the run is live and from
              the run directory after it (LESSONS.md "Transcripts are written outside the worker's reach")
  -f          follow: keep printing new events as they arrive (Ctrl-C to leave; the run is not affected)
  --last N    start from the last N events instead of the beginning
  --full      do not truncate file contents, command output or written files
  --thinking  show the model's visible thinking text where the log carries it
```

## Lessons it cites

- → **Transcripts are written outside the worker's reach**
- → **Networked and Codex launches need their flags bound**

## Ledger events it writes

None.
